facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) with data injection uses a real final or representative ECU and its I/O, often running production software.
facts.quote: **What is real:** the final or representative ECU and its I/O, often running production software.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) with data injection needs a real-time simulator with deterministic timing, a machine-dynamics model, electrical I/O and sensor-interface emulation, restbus models for the rest of the machine network, and the ISO/TS 21815-2 brake-request interface.
facts.quote: restbus models for the rest of the machine network; and the ISO/TS 21815-2 brake-request interface. **Independent** [3].

facts.text: Sensor-interface and electrical I/O emulation for HIL data injection can use camera RAW-data injection behind the imager, radar detection-level injection, and recorded J1939 or CAN traffic.
facts.quote: electrical I/O and sensor-interface emulation (camera RAW-data injection behind the imager, radar detection-level injection, recorded J1939 or CAN traffic)

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop with data injection is closed-loop when actuator outputs feed the simulation.
facts.quote: Closed-loop when actuator outputs feed the simulation.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop with data injection proves real-time behaviour of the production ECU and target binary, communications and interface timing, diagnostic and fault behaviour, fail-to-safe behaviour, and decision and control logic under repeatable scenarios.
facts.quote: **Proves:** real-time behaviour of the production ECU, the target binary, communications and interface timing, diagnostic and fault behaviour, fail-to-safe behaviour, and decision and control logic under repeatable scenarios.

facts.text: MOSH requires a disconnection between the detection device and the machine to be detected within 500 ms.
facts.quote: MOSH requires, for example, that a disconnection between the detection device and the machine be detected within 500 ms

facts.text: MOSH requires the machine to reply within 50 ms.
facts.quote: and that the machine reply within 50 ms. **Independent** [17].

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop with data injection cannot prove sensor front-end behaviour because injection bypasses the optics, lens, imager and possibly the image signal processor.
facts.quote: **Cannot prove:** sensor front-end behaviour, because injection bypasses the optics, lens, imager and possibly the image signal processor

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop with data injection cannot prove true machine and brake behaviour when the machine and brakes are entirely modeled.
facts.quote: true machine and brake behaviour when these are entirely modeled.

facts.text: Vendor systems demonstrate multi-I/O, synchronized, closed-loop HIL with synthetic camera input and fault injection for automotive driver assistance; this is vendor on-road evidence.
facts.quote: vendor systems demonstrate multi-I/O, synchronized, closed-loop HIL with synthetic camera input and fault injection for automotive driver assistance. **Vendor (on-road evidence)** [41].
